status: Brotli decoder and local reader integration verified; cloud validation and remaining audit work are still open
contract: Caller supplies exact output; declared metablock output is checked before growing ring backing. No chunk accumulation or final output concatenation.

Per-call workspace slots reuse backing across metablocks. Growth is charged before allocation/copy; old backing releases afterward. All scratch backing releases on success, malformed input or budget rejection.

Scoped codec charges output, conservative decoder-state metadata, workspace backing and slot/view metadata. Module-level static dictionary and lookup tables are shared storage outside per-call accounting.
Fixed output validates complete input consumption, including trailing bytes beyond the bit-reader buffer. Overlapping input/output rejects before workspace allocation.
Brotli does not claim a complete fixed header-only workspace forecast. Existing generic incremental scoped decoding is used.

tests: Node Brotli encoder produces independent compressed bytes across qualities 0,1,4,11; empty, dictionary text, raw blocks and ring wrapping decode exactly.
All truncated prefixes, short/long declared outputs, trailing bytes, overlap and offset-view sentinels checked.
Measured exact workspace bound succeeds; one byte below fails without retained allocations. Scoped output survives until scope disposal.
Actual generated Brotli Parquet pages: INT32 and nullable UTF-8, multiple groups/pages, public and owned readers, batch sizes 1/64/256.
Actual external large_string_map.brotli.parquet rejects under 64 and 128 MiB in scoped public batches and owned queries; pool returns to zero.

conformanceContractChange: Previously both huge-fixture cases expected successful unbounded materialization. Tests now inspect actual page-header extents, independent of codec/file names: pages above the 64 MiB test cap must produce LAKEQL_BUDGET_EXCEEDED and release allocations. Large columns composed of smaller pages still require successful value/row-count parity. Unsupported-codec preflight tests use LZO now that Brotli is supported; rejection assertions remain intact.
remaining: Native Worker R2/cloud HTTP concurrency and cache lifetime proof for Brotli.
Brotli throughput, scaling and bundle-cost measurements; no speedup is claimed.
Full release gates and broader F1-F6/M1-M2/V1-V3 audit requirements remain active.
Accounting is not total heap/RSS or hosted Cloudflare memory-cap certification. Public unscoped reads retain their caller-managed materialization contract.
